purpose: Compare Methodome's computational method capability with the methodology corpus without conflating numerical implementation correctness, source support, and expert-benchmark validation.

status_definitions.source_supported: A source-backed operational decision rule exists and has passed corpus consistency review; expert-labelled methodology benchmark validation is still pending.
status_definitions.source_supported_concept: The method family/design distinction is source-backed, but autonomous model-specific selection or execution is intentionally outside v1.
status_definitions.deferred: Known branch intentionally held outside v1 autonomous recommendation/execution.
status_definitions.executable: The current deterministic runtime can calculate the method when explicitly selected.
status_definitions.non_executable: The current deterministic runtime does not calculate the method.

principles: Computational validation asks whether an implementation returns correct numerical results for a specified method.
Methodological validation asks whether Methodome selected, rejected, interpreted and diagnosed the method appropriately for the question, estimand, design, measurement structure and data conditions.
Source-supported does not mean expert-benchmark validated.
No method is promoted to methodology-validated status until it passes the planned expert-labelled protocol-to-analysis benchmark.
A non-executable method can still have source-supported routing rules that tell Methodome when to stop, warn or defer rather than make a bad recommendation.

methods.finding: Variable-type routing, categorical counts/proportions and distribution-aware quantitative summaries are source-supported.
methods.action: Keep executable; validate autonomous summary choices against expert-labelled cases.

methods.finding: Linear quantitative association plus form/outlier checks are source-supported.
methods.action: Keep executable inside the independence/design boundary.

methods.finding: Ordinal/ranked and monotonic association routing is source-supported, with explicit rejection of a normality-p-value auto-switch.
methods.action: Keep executable; benchmark monotonicity, repeated-observation and interpretation gates.

methods.finding: Categorical eligibility and expected-count approximation checks are source-supported.
methods.action: Keep executable with exact-test routing where appropriate.

methods.finding: Independent sparse 2x2 exact testing is source-supported without an arbitrary overall sample-size cutoff.
methods.action: Keep executable; dependence/cluster/survey structures remain blockers.

methods.finding: Quantitative-outcome eligibility, LINE assumptions, residual diagnostics and multicollinearity safeguards are source-supported.
methods.action: Keep executable inside the current iid/design boundary.

methods.finding: Binary-response routing, fit/residual diagnostics, complete/quasi-complete separation safeguards and sparse-event safeguards are source-supported. A universal 10-EPV gate is explicitly rejected.
methods.action: Keep executable ordinary ML only when safeguards do not place the fit outside its reliability boundary; Firth remains non-executable.

methods.finding: Independent two-group mean comparison and Welch-versus-pooled logic are source-supported without a universal n>=30 rule.
methods.action: Candidate for the next deterministic executor expansion.

methods.finding: Paired analysis based on within-pair differences is source-supported.
methods.action: Candidate for the next deterministic executor expansion.

methods.finding: Ordinary one-way fixed-effect ANOVA is source-supported only after design and residual-structure checks; repeated/random/clustered structures are blocked.
methods.action: Candidate for deterministic executor expansion after design gate is wired.

methods.finding: Paired rank inference with a symmetry requirement for the usual signed-rank interpretation is source-supported.
methods.action: Candidate for later executor expansion.

methods.finding: Rank/distribution comparison is source-supported; generic 'test of medians' and 'non-normal t-test' interpretations are explicitly blocked.
methods.action: Candidate for later executor expansion after estimand/interpretation tests are benchmarked.

methods.finding: Independent multi-group rank comparison is source-supported with design and interpretation safeguards.
methods.action: Candidate for later executor expansion.

methods.finding: Complex-survey weights, strata, PSUs and domain variance handling are source-supported, but no survey executor is active.
methods.action: Block iid inference when design metadata requires survey-aware analysis; implement later.

methods.finding: Correlation-aware subject-specific modelling is source-supported conceptually.
methods.action: Keep non-executable until model-specific eligibility/diagnostics and numerical implementation are added.

methods.finding: Population-average/marginal interpretation is source-supported conceptually.
methods.action: Keep non-executable; resolve target estimand and small-cluster safeguards before activation.

methods.finding: Count routing and mean-variance/overdispersion principles are source-supported, but operational dispersion remediation and advanced count-model routing are deferred.
methods.action: Do not autonomously execute/recommend in v1.

methods.finding: The corpus explicitly rejects automatic overdispersion→negative-binomial switching; detailed selection is deferred.
methods.action: Do not autonomously execute/recommend in v1.

methods.finding: Sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, likelihood ratios and threshold behaviour are source-supported.
methods.action: Recognize and plan the workflow, but keep numerical diagnostic pipeline outside v1 runtime.

methods.finding: Competing events must not be treated as ordinary noninformative censoring; target estimand determines cause-specific versus subdistribution family.
methods.action: Block ordinary survival-only routing when competing risks are present.

methods.finding: Causal identification assumptions and difference-in-differences parallel-trend logic are source-supported, but estimator-specific autonomous execution is outside v1.
methods.action: Use the causal gate to prevent adjusted association models from being mislabeled causal.

methods.finding: Reflective/formative structure, structural validity before internal consistency, and reliability versus measurement error are source-supported.
methods.action: Recognize and safeguard psychometric questions; full factor/reliability/invariance execution remains future work.

methods.finding: Pretrend, level/slope change and autocorrelation requirements are source-supported.
methods.action: Block simple pre/post substitution; executor deferred.
